question: The modern-day __________ was molded by the renowned Tanjore Bandhu, consisting of the four Nattuvanars: Ponnayya, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnayya.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Modern-day Bharatanatyam was shaped/standardised in the 19th century by the Tanjore (Thanjavur) Quartet — the four Nattuvanar brothers Ponnayya, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnayya — who systematised its repertoire (the Margam sequence: Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, Padam, Tillana). (भरतनाट्यम — तंजौर चौकड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms, originating in the temples of Tamil Nadu (earlier called Sadir / Dasiattam), and is based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni.

• It is characterised by the araimandi (half-sitting posture), mudras (hand gestures), and abhinaya (expression), and combines nritta (pure dance), nritya (expressive dance) and natya (drama).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Who became the first female armless archer to win a medal at the Para World Championship event, 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sheetal Devi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sheetal Devi, a para-archer from Jammu & Kashmir, became the first female armless archer to win a medal at the World Archery Para Championship, 2023. Born with a condition affecting her arms, she shoots using her legs and shoulder. (शीतल देवी — आर्मलेस पैरा तीरंदाज़)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• At the Asian Para Games 2023 (Hangzhou), Sheetal Devi won two gold medals and one bronze, becoming the first Indian woman to win two golds at a single Asian Para Games.

• She later won a bronze at the Paris 2024 Paralympics (mixed team compound).

NOTE

• Para sports for the differently-abled are governed globally by the International Paralympic Committee (IPC); the Paralympic Games are held after the Olympics in the same host city.

question: Which of the following options represents the correct flow of energy in an ecosystem?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sunlight → Producers → Herbivores → Carnivores.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Energy flows through an ecosystem in a single direction: the Sun is the ultimate source; producers (green plants) capture solar energy by photosynthesis; herbivores (primary consumers) eat plants; and carnivores (secondary/tertiary consumers) eat herbivores. (ऊर्जा प्रवाह — सूर्य → उत्पादक → शाकाहारी → मांसाहारी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The flow of energy is unidirectional (it does not cycle back), and at each trophic level only about 10% of energy is passed on — the "10 percent law" given by Lindeman.

• A food chain shows this transfer; interconnected food chains form a food web.

NOTE

• Trophic levels: Producers (T1) → Herbivores/Primary consumers (T2) → Small carnivores/Secondary consumers (T3) → Top carnivores/Tertiary consumers (T4). Decomposers (bacteria, fungi) recycle nutrients back to the soil.

question: At 10 × 10⁴ Pa pressure and 300 K temperature, the volume of 0.09 mol CO₂ gas is 22.4 × 10⁻³ m³. What will be the volume of the gas if the pressure is decreased to 2 × 10⁴ Pa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 112.0 × 10⁻³ m³.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At constant temperature, this is a case of Boyle's Law, which states that the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its volume (P₁V₁ = P₂V₂). (बॉयल का नियम)

• Calculation:

◦ P₁V₁ = P₂V₂

◦ (10 × 10⁴) × (22.4 × 10⁻³) = (2 × 10⁴) × V₂

◦ V₂ = [(10 × 10⁴) × (22.4 × 10⁻³)] ÷ (2 × 10⁴) = 22.4 × 10⁻³ × 5 = 112.0 × 10⁻³ m³.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• As the pressure is reduced to one-fifth (from 10×10⁴ to 2×10⁴ Pa), the volume increases five times, confirming the inverse relationship.

• Charles's Law: at constant pressure, V ∝ T. Gay-Lussac's Law: at constant volume, P ∝ T. Combined: PV/T = constant (Ideal Gas Equation: PV = nRT).

NOTE

• Boyle's Law is valid at constant temperature and fixed amount of gas; the temperature 300 K here stays constant, so only P and V change.

question: In 1990, who established Nrityagram, a dance school in Bengaluru?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Protima Gauri Bedi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nrityagram, a dance village/school near Bengaluru (Hesaraghatta), Karnataka, was founded in 1990 by the celebrated Odissi dancer Protima Gauri Bedi (Protima Bedi). (नृत्यग्राम — प्रोतिमा गौरी बेदी)

• It was conceived as a residential "gurukul" where students live and train in classical dance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Protima Bedi learnt Odissi under Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra.

• Nrityagram was designed by the award-winning architect Gerard da Cunha.

• After Protima's death (1998, in a Himalayan landslide), the institution has been led by dancers such as Surupa Sen and Bijayini Satpathy.

NOTE

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha, known for the tribhanga (three-bend) posture and chowk stance, with themes from the Gita Govinda of Jayadeva.

question: The __________ scheme, that covers artisans related to 18 fields, was included under the 'Payments Infrastructure Development Fund' ('PIDF') scheme by the Reserve Bank of India in October 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM Vishwakarma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Beneficiaries of the PM Vishwakarma scheme — which covers 18 trades/fields of traditional artisans and craftspeople — were brought under the Payments Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) of the RBI in October 2023 to boost their digital payment acceptance. (पीएम विश्वकर्मा योजना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• PM Vishwakarma was launched on 17 September 2023 by the Ministry of MSME. It provides skill training, a toolkit incentive, and collateral-free credit to artisans such as carpenters, blacksmiths, goldsmiths, potters, cobblers, tailors, barbers, boat-makers, etc.

• The PIDF was set up by the RBI in 2021 to expand payment infrastructure (PoS terminals, QR codes) in tier-3 to tier-6 centres and the North-East.

NOTE

• Related schemes: PM SVANidhi (street vendors), PM USHA (higher education/universities), PM Ullas / ULLAS (adult literacy — "New India Literacy Programme").

question: Who among the following formed an organisation to support widow remarriage in Madras Presidency?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Veereshlingam Pantulu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kandukuri Veeresalingam Pantulu was a great social reformer of the Madras Presidency (Andhra region) who championed widow remarriage and founded organisations/associations to promote it. He performed the first widow remarriage in the region in 1881. (कंदुकुरी वीरेशलिंगम पंतुलु — विधवा पुनर्विवाह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He is regarded as the "father of the Telugu Renaissance" and worked for women's education and against social evils like dowry and the nautch system.

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar led the movement for widow remarriage in Bengal, resulting in the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856.

NOTE

• Key social reformers for SSC: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Sati abolition, 1829; Brahmo Samaj), Vidyasagar (widow remarriage), Jyotiba Phule (women/depressed classes), Dayananda Saraswati (Arya Samaj).

question: Which of the following Articles entails "Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 16.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 16 of the Constitution guarantees "Equality of opportunity in matters of public employment" — no citizen shall be discriminated against in government jobs on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth or residence. (अनुच्छेद 16 — लोक नियोजन में अवसर की समता)

• It also permits reservation in appointments for backward classes (SC/ST/OBC) not adequately represented.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 14 — Equality before law and equal protection of laws.

• Article 15 — Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

• Article 17 — Abolition of untouchability.

• Article 18 — Abolition of titles.

NOTE

• Articles 14 to 18 together form the Right to Equality, part of the Fundamental Rights (Part III) of the Constitution.

question: Sawai Gandharva was associated with which of the following gharanas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana gharana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sawai Gandharva (Rambhau Kundgolkar) was a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana gharana. He was a disciple of Ustad Abdul Karim Khan, the founder of the gharana. (किराना घराना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sawai Gandharva's famous disciples include Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal and Firoz Dastur.

• The annual "Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav" music festival in Pune is held in his memory.

• The Kirana gharana is known for its emphasis on melody, precise intonation (swara) and slow, elaborate raga development.

NOTE

• Major gharanas of Hindustani vocal music: Gwalior (oldest), Kirana, Agra, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala and Banaras.

question: The partition of __________ was annulled in 1911.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Partition of Bengal, carried out by Lord Curzon in 1905, was annulled (reversed) in 1911 at the Delhi Durbar by King George V, largely due to the strong Swadeshi Movement and widespread protests. (बंगाल विभाजन — 1905, रद्द 1911)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 1905 partition split Bengal into West Bengal (Hindu-majority) and East Bengal & Assam (Muslim-majority); Indians saw it as a "divide and rule" policy.

• The annulment came along with the shifting of the capital of British India from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911.

• The Swadeshi and Boycott movements (using Indian goods, boycotting British goods) grew out of the anti-partition agitation.

NOTE

• Bengal was again partitioned along religious lines during India's Independence in 1947 (into West Bengal, India, and East Pakistan, now Bangladesh).

question: Who is the author of 'The story of My Experiments with Truth'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is MK Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Story of My Experiments with Truth" is the autobiography of Mahatma Gandhi (Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi). It was originally written in Gujarati and covers his life up to the 1920s. (सत्य के प्रयोग — महात्मा गांधी की आत्मकथा)

• It was translated into English by Mahadev Desai.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Gandhiji also wrote "Hind Swaraj" (1909) and edited journals like Young India, Harijan and Navajivan.

• He is called the "Father of the Nation" and led movements such as Non-Cooperation (1920), Civil Disobedience/Dandi March (1930) and Quit India (1942).

NOTE

• Famous autobiographies: *An Autobiography / Toward Freedom* (Jawaharlal Nehru), *Autobiography of a Yogi* (Paramahansa Yogananda), *Wings of Fire* (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), *My Experiments with Truth* (Gandhi).

question: Which state in India has the largest scheduled tribe population as per the 2011 Census?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, Madhya Pradesh has the largest Scheduled Tribe (ST) population among Indian states (about 1.53 crore). (मध्य प्रदेश — सर्वाधिक अनुसूचित जनजाति जनसंख्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• After Madhya Pradesh, the states with large ST populations are Maharashtra, Odisha and Rajasthan.

• In terms of the percentage of ST population, Mizoram, Nagaland and Meghalaya rank highest; among UTs, Lakshadweep.

• Major tribes of MP: Gond, Bhil, Baiga, Korku, Sahariya.

NOTE

• Scheduled Tribes are notified under Article 342; their welfare is looked after by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. India's overall ST population is about 8.6% of the total.

question: In which state is the Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Power Project located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Power Project, one of the largest single-site solar plants in India (750 MW), is located in the Rewa district of Madhya Pradesh. (रीवा अल्ट्रा मेगा सोलर पार्क — मध्य प्रदेश)

• Power from Rewa notably supplies the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other major solar parks in India: Bhadla Solar Park (Rajasthan) — the world's largest, Pavagada Solar Park (Karnataka) and Kurnool (Andhra Pradesh).

• Solar energy is a renewable, non-conventional source of energy; India's solar push is driven by the National Solar Mission and the International Solar Alliance (ISA), headquartered at Gurugram.

NOTE

• India aims for 500 GW of non-fossil-fuel energy capacity by 2030 (a commitment made at the COP-26 Glasgow summit).

question: As per Census 2011, which of the following is the most populated city in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, Mumbai (Greater Mumbai) in Maharashtra was the most populated city in India, with a population of over 1.24 crore. (मुंबई — सर्वाधिक जनसंख्या वाला शहर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• After Mumbai, the most populous cities (2011) were Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Chennai.

• Mumbai is the financial capital of India, home to the RBI, BSE, NSE and the film industry (Bollywood).

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th census of India and the 7th after independence. The most populous state is Uttar Pradesh.

question: In the State Legislature, _______ is subject to dissolution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Legislative Assembly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a State Legislature, the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is the lower house and is subject to dissolution. Its normal term is five years, but it can be dissolved earlier by the Governor. (विधान सभा — विघटन के अधीन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is the upper house at the state level; like the Rajya Sabha, it is a permanent body and is NOT subject to dissolution (one-third of its members retire every two years).

• "Council of States" = Rajya Sabha and "House of People" = Lok Sabha — these belong to the Union Parliament, not the State Legislature.

NOTE

• Only some states have a Legislative Council (bicameral), e.g., UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh. The Council is created/abolished under Article 169.

question: What is the chemical name for the compound responsible for the cooling sensation in mint leaves?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Menthol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Menthol" is the organic compound (an alcohol) found in mint (peppermint) leaves that produces the characteristic cooling sensation. It works by activating the cold-sensitive receptors (TRPM8) of the skin/mouth. (मेन्थॉल — पुदीना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ethanol — the alcohol in alcoholic drinks and sanitisers.

• Caffeine — the stimulant in tea and coffee.

• Capsaicin — the compound in chillies responsible for their hot, pungent sensation (opposite of menthol's cooling effect).

NOTE

• Menthol is widely used in toothpastes, balms, cough drops, mouth fresheners and pain-relief ointments for its cooling and mild anaesthetic effect.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct?

A) Harappan culture spread only to Sindh and Punjab.  B) The script of the Harappan culture has been deciphered by historians.  C) At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.  D) Granaries in the Indus Valley Civilization were found in Harappa only.
option_1: Harappan culture spread only to Sindh and Punjab.
option_2: The script of the Harappan culture has been deciphered by historians.
option_3: At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits.
option_4: Granaries in the Indus Valley Civilization were found in Harappa only.
solution_text:
The correct answer is At burials in Harappan sites the dead were generally laid in pits (Option 3).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilization, the dead were generally buried in pits, usually laid in a north–south direction, often with grave goods like pottery and ornaments. Hence statement C is correct. (हड़प्पा — गड्ढों में दफनाना)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Statement A is wrong: the Harappan culture was very widespread — extending into Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, western UP, Sindh, Punjab, Baluchistan and Afghanistan — not only Sindh and Punjab.

• Statement B is wrong: the Harappan script is still undeciphered (it is pictographic and written boustrophedon — right to left, then left to right).

• Statement D is wrong: granaries were found at multiple sites — the "Great Granary" at Mohenjo-daro and granaries at Harappa, among others.

NOTE

• Key Harappan features: town planning on a grid, the Great Bath (Mohenjo-daro), advanced drainage, standardised burnt bricks, seals (e.g., the Pashupati seal) and a script that remains unread.

question: To control the prices, which of the following Sultans of Delhi set up three different markets for different commodities in Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alauddin Khalji.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Alauddin Khalji (r. 1296–1316) introduced famous market/price control reforms in Delhi, setting up separate markets for different commodities — the Mandi (grain market), the Sarai Adl (cloth and manufactured goods market), and markets for horses, cattle and slaves. (अलाउद्दीन खिलजी — बाज़ार नियंत्रण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He appointed officers like the Shahna-i-Mandi (market superintendent), Diwan-i-Riyasat and Barids (spies) to enforce fixed prices.

• These reforms were mainly to maintain a large standing army at low cost and to check hoarding.

• He also introduced the Dagh (branding of horses) and Chehra (descriptive roll of soldiers) systems.

NOTE

• The five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526): Slave/Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi. Alauddin Khalji also repelled several Mongol invasions.

question: The second largest dome in the world was built in India and is still standing strong. Which dome is being spoken about here?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gol Gumbaz.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gol Gumbaz, located at Bijapur (Vijayapura), Karnataka, is famous for having one of the largest domes in the world (often cited as the second largest). It is the mausoleum (tomb) of Muhammad Adil Shah of the Adil Shahi dynasty of Bijapur. (गोल गुम्बज — बीजापुर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gol Gumbaz is renowned for its "Whispering Gallery", where even a faint sound is echoed and heard clearly across the dome.

• It was built in the 17th century and is a fine example of Deccan (Indo-Islamic) architecture.

NOTE

• "Gol Gumbaz" literally means "circular dome". Its dome stands without any pillars supporting it, an engineering marvel of its time.

question: For which of the following minerals are Jharia and Raniganj known?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jharia (Jharkhand) and Raniganj (West Bengal) are among India's oldest and most important coalfields. (झरिया एवं रानीगंज — कोयला)

• Jharia is especially famous for coking (bituminous) coal, used in the iron and steel industry.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Most of India's coal reserves lie in the Gondwana rock system in the Damodar valley (Jharkhand–West Bengal).

• Other major coalfields: Bokaro, Giridih (Jharkhand), Korba (Chhattisgarh), Singrauli (MP) and Talcher (Odisha).

• Coal is called "black gold" and is a major source of thermal power in India.

NOTE

• Types of coal by carbon content (highest to lowest): Anthracite > Bituminous > Lignite > Peat. Jharia mines have long suffered from underground coal fires.

question: Identify the correct match in the context of microfinance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Yunus - Grameen Bank - Bangladesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Professor Muhammad Yunus founded the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh in 1983, pioneering the concept of microcredit / microfinance — providing small, collateral-free loans to the rural poor, especially women. (मुहम्मद यूनुस — ग्रामीण बैंक — बांग्लादेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Muhammad Yunus and the Grameen Bank were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 for their efforts to create economic and social development from below.

• The Grameen model of group lending and joint liability inspired Self Help Groups (SHGs) and microfinance institutions in India.

NOTE

• In India, microfinance is supported by the NABARD SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (1992) and regulated by the RBI. Yunus is often called the "Banker to the Poor".

question: What was the name of the official torch for the Khelo India University Games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shakti.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The official torch of the Khelo India University Games 2022 (held in 2023) was named "Shakti", symbolising strength and energy. (खेलो इंडिया यूनिवर्सिटी गेम्स 2022 — मशाल 'शक्ति')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Khelo India University Games (KIUG) are a part of the Khelo India programme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to promote sports at the grassroots and university level.

• The 2022 edition was hosted mainly by Uttar Pradesh.

NOTE

• The Khelo India scheme includes the Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India University Games and Khelo India Winter Games, aimed at identifying and nurturing young sporting talent.

question: In March 2023, who was appointed as Chairperson of Pension Fund Regulatory Development Authority (PFRDA)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Deepak Mohanty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Deepak Mohanty was appointed the Chairperson of the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) in March 2023. (दीपक मोहंती — पीएफआरडीए अध्यक्ष)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The PFRDA is a statutory regulatory body (established under the PFRDA Act, 2013) that regulates the National Pension System (NPS) and pension schemes in India. Its headquarters are in New Delhi.

• Other regulators for SSC: RBI (banking/monetary), SEBI (securities market), IRDAI (insurance).

NOTE

• The NPS is a voluntary, defined-contribution retirement savings scheme; the Atal Pension Yojana (APY) for the unorganised sector is also administered under PFRDA.

question: Losar festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Losar" is the New Year festival of the Buddhist communities (such as the Monpa tribe) of Arunachal Pradesh; it is also celebrated in Ladakh, Sikkim and Himachal (Spiti/Lahaul). (लोसर महोत्सव — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

• It marks the beginning of the Tibetan/Buddhist new year and is celebrated with prayers, dances and feasting.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other festivals of Arunachal Pradesh: Solung, Mopin, Nyokum, Dree and Reh.

• Losar usually falls in February–March, according to the lunar calendar.

NOTE

• Arunachal Pradesh, the "Land of the Dawn-lit Mountains", is India's easternmost state; its capital is Itanagar. It became a full state in 1987.

question: The percentage of pore space between the particles inside a rock or soil is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Porosity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Porosity" is the percentage of pore (empty) space between the particles inside a rock or soil — it measures how much water or air the rock/soil can hold. (सरंध्रता / पोरोसिटी)

◦ Porosity = (Volume of pores ÷ Total volume) × 100.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Permeability" is different — it is the ability of a rock/soil to allow water to pass through it. A rock can be porous but not very permeable (e.g., clay holds water but does not let it flow easily).

• "Density" is mass per unit volume; "salinity" is the salt content of water/soil.

NOTE

• Aquifers (water-bearing rocks) need both high porosity and high permeability (e.g., sandstone) to store and yield groundwater effectively. Clay is porous but poorly permeable.
